title: Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI / PORT)
sources: Fine MJ et al. NEJM 1997 (PORT cohort); ATS/IDSA 2019 CAP guideline

changelog.change: Converted to the formula engine so the age term (age, minus 10 for women) is actually summed — the previous additive build left age contributing 0. Point weights unchanged and verified against the spec.

purpose: Stratifies 30-day mortality in community-acquired pneumonia to support the admit-vs-discharge decision. More discriminating than CURB-65 but more complex (needs labs and an ABG). The score is the patient's age in years (minus 10 for women) plus the weighted points below.

inputs.label: Neoplastic disease (active cancer, excl. basal/squamous skin)
Renal disease (chronic kidney disease / abnormal baseline creatinine)

formulas.label: PSI / PORT score
formulas.expression: age - 10 * sex + nursingHome + neoplasm + liver + chf + cva + renal + ams + rr30 + sbp90 + temp + pulse125 + ph + bun + sodium + glucose + hct + pao2 + effusion

interpretation.label: Class I–II (≤ 70) — 30-day mortality ~ 0.1–1.0%. Outpatient treatment. (Class I proper is age < 50 with none of the listed comorbidities or exam abnormalities — a low score approximates it.)
Class III (71–90) — 30-day mortality ~ 0.9–3.8%. Brief observation unit or short admission

Class V (> 130) — 30-day mortality ~ 16.8–38.3%. Inpatient admission; assess for ICU (ATS/IDSA minor criteria, or a major criterion — septic shock on pressors, or respiratory failure needing ventilation)

notes: The score is age (−10 if female) plus the weighted points. PSI can under-triage a young patient with few comorbidities but real physiologic derangement — always overlay clinical judgement, hypoxaemia, ability to take oral medication, and social factors. CURB-65 is the quicker bedside alternative (no labs). Neither score decides ICU admission — that is the ATS/IDSA criteria.
buildNote: Formula engine — total = age (−10 if female) + weighted select points. Five risk classes per Fine 1997; mortality ranges per the derivation cohort.
